meta.title: RetailCo Store Risk-to-Action Proposal
meta.subtitle: Following one store through one day, before and after live operating intelligence

slides.title: RetailCo Store Risk-to-Action Proposal
slides.subtitle: One store, one day: from Monday-lag visibility to same-day operating control
slides.script: We should not treat the Monday spreadsheet as an inconvenience. Across 120 stores and 2,000 frontline staff, delayed visibility is an operating exposure. Brand standards, compliance habits, customer experience and manager capability are all being created store by store, conversation by conversation, without a reliable way to see them while they still matter. We are going to follow one store through a normal day, show where the risk enters, and then show how Spacesight, Echo, AI Wiki and Alivia turn that same day into action.

slides.title: Where we are taking this
bullets: Show the same day after instrumentation
Map each COO concern to a product
Ask for a small named-store pilot
slides.script: We will keep this very concrete. Rather than walk through products in isolation, we will follow a single RetailCo store from opening to close. First, we will look at what happens today when the only reliable view arrives the following Monday. Then we will replay the same day with live floor visibility, conversation capture and a searchable playbook. Finally, we will be explicit about coverage, including the rostering pain, and we will ask for a small pilot in named stores rather than a broad transformation commitment.

slides.quote: I have no idea what actually happens on my shop floor. I get a spreadsheet on Monday about last week.
slides.script: We hear this as the central risk statement. If a store opens on Tuesday and something changes on the floor, the operating system does not really know until the following Monday. That is too late for customer recovery, coaching, compliance correction or understanding why one store feels different from another. Spacesight is the product that answers this directly. It gives RetailCo a way to see what is actually happening on the shop floor as an operating signal, not as a post-mortem buried in a spreadsheet.

slides.text: Across 120 stores, last-week visibility turns daily operating drift into brand, compliance and customer-experience exposure.
slides.script: We are framing the first hour of the day as exposure because normal trading creates risk quietly. A fixture is missed, a queue forms, a team member is pulled away from the floor, or a manager improvises in a way that works in one store but breaks in another. None of that is automatically bad, but it is unmanaged if RetailCo cannot see it. Spacesight changes the posture from retrospective reporting to same-day awareness, so store operations can be managed while the customer experience is still happening.

slides.title: 09:15 — the risk is not dramatic, it is ordinary
slides.statement: The store can look open, staffed and trading while the important exceptions remain invisible.
bullets: Customer flow changes before reports notice
Service moments happen without a record
slides.script: We are not suggesting every store is failing. The risk is that RetailCo cannot reliably distinguish healthy variation from harmful drift. Spacesight covers the visible operating layer by showing what is happening on the floor. Echo covers the service layer by capturing and scoring what staff actually say to customers. Together they create a same-day evidence base. That means the conversation with stores changes from opinion and anecdotes to specific patterns: what happened, where it happened, and what the manager or team can do next.

slides.quote: My best store managers outsell my worst ones by 3x. I cannot bottle what they do.
slides.script: We would treat the 3x manager gap as both opportunity and risk. It means RetailCo already has high-performing practice inside the estate, but that practice is trapped in individual managers and local habits. Echo helps identify the customer conversations that strong teams are having. Spacesight helps identify the floor behaviours around those moments. AI Wiki then becomes the way to bottle the repeatable parts, so the best manager’s approach is no longer something people have to absorb by luck, proximity or tenure.

slides.label: Performance gap between best and worst store managers
slides.script: We do not need to invent value here because RetailCo has already named it. A 3x spread says the playbook is uneven. The question is how to make the strongest behaviours observable, teachable and reusable without asking the best managers to personally coach 120 stores. Echo turns live customer interactions into examples that can be scored. Spacesight adds the operating context around those interactions. AI Wiki turns the examples, guidance and store routines into a searchable source that a manager or new hire can use during the working week.

slides.title: 12:30 — the same store after instrumentation

rows.right: Echo captures and scores real interactions

slides.script: By midday, the before-and-after becomes practical. In the current model, the store is generating signals, but those signals are mostly lost or delayed. With Spacesight, RetailCo sees floor patterns the same day. With Echo, the service interaction is no longer hearsay. With AI Wiki, the good practice discovered in one store becomes available to another store. Alivia then turns the findings and recommendations into a structured client proposal, so the pilot does not end as a pile of observations; it becomes an actionable RetailCo plan.

slides.quote: Onboarding a new hire takes six weeks and depends entirely on whoever happens to be working that day.
slides.script: We see onboarding as the human version of the same risk. If a new hire’s first six weeks depend on whoever is rostered, RetailCo is not really onboarding through a system; it is onboarding through chance. AI Wiki addresses this directly by giving the new hire and the store manager a consistent place to find the RetailCo way of working. Echo can contribute real examples of good customer conversations. Spacesight can contribute store-floor practices. The result is not generic training; it is the bottled practice of RetailCo’s own best stores.

slides.title: 17:00 — coverage map, including the honest open item

rows.right: Spacesight provides same-day in-store vision analytics.
Echo captures and scores what staff actually say.
AI Wiki turns proven practice into a searchable guide.
Open item: Alivia scopes rostering integration and operating handoffs.

slides.script: We want to be clear about what is covered and what is not. Spacesight, Echo and AI Wiki directly address the visibility, conversation, manager-gap and onboarding problems. Scheduling is different. None of these products is a dedicated workforce management scheduler, so we should not pretend it replaces your rostering system. What we can do is use Alivia to define the adjacent play: what data should flow into rostering, which handoffs create pain, and how the pilot should specify integration or process changes with RetailCo’s existing scheduling environment.

slides.title: Let’s name three pilot stores this week
slides.subtitle: A focused store-day pilot: one top performer, one mid-pack store, one low performer.
bullets: Run Spacesight, Echo and AI Wiki around one store day
Use Alivia to produce the pilot proposal and open-items plan
Review findings with the COO team
slides.script: Our ask is deliberately small and named. We should pick three APAC stores together this week: one store that already performs strongly, one middle store, and one lower-performing store. That gives us contrast without trying to instrument the whole estate at once. We will use Spacesight, Echo and AI Wiki to follow the store day, then use Alivia to package the evidence, recommendations and the rostering open item into a clear proposal. From there, RetailCo can decide with evidence, not with Monday’s spreadsheet.

approach.angle: Frame it as risk. Not knowing what happens across the estate is an exposure - brand, compliance, customer experience - not just an inconvenience.
approach.device: Follow one store through a single day, before and after.
approach.opener: Open with a short agenda so the COO knows exactly where you are taking them.
approach.close: Close by asking for a pilot in a small, named set of stores.
